1: # Responsive media editor with video audio removal
2: 
3: ## Version boundary
4: 
5: Implement the media-editor behavior introduced between Signal Android v8.22.2 (`e3a7a9c8764bf5961bbbb54f5d72d1056dd3974e`) and v8.23.0 (`64fa9f50a38fecb088135fd0200c331fe0686bd3`).
6: 
7: ## User outcome
8: 
9: Users can review and edit one or more selected media items in an editor that remains usable across phone, tablet, and foldable layouts. For an ordinary video, they can remove its audio before sending while keeping edits attached to the correct item throughout the send flow.
10: 
11: ## Functional requirements
12: 
13: - Keep the editor's selection, focused item, ordering, message metadata, and per-item edits synchronized with the enclosing media-send flow. Changing focus or reordering items must not transfer one item's edits to another item.
14: - Restore editor state after recreation so selected media, focus, and completed edits do not silently reset.
15: - Offer audio removal only for an editable video. Do not offer it for images, documents, or video-GIF items.
16: - Toggling audio removal updates only the focused video's edit state. Toggling it again restores audio, and selecting another item reveals that item's own setting.
17: - Give immediate user feedback when a video becomes muted.
18: - Treat a first video edit as invalidating any pre-uploaded version of that item so the eventual send cannot use stale media.
19: - Carry trim and audio-removal choices through attachment preparation and video processing. A muted video must retain its video track and omit its audio track in the sent output.
20: - Preserve backward compatibility for stored attachment transforms that predate audio removal; missing audio-removal data must behave as unmuted.
21: - When closing a flow that still contains selected media, ask before discarding it. Confirming exits and discards the pending work; canceling keeps the flow and all edits intact.
22: - In a camera-first flow with only the just-captured item selected, backing out of the editor discards that capture and returns to the camera rather than leaving an empty editor.
23: 
24: ## Invariants
25: 
26: - Edit state is keyed to media identity, not pager position.
27: - Audio removal defaults to off and never applies to unsupported media types.
28: - Reordering or changing focus does not change media membership or edit contents.
29: - Sending uses the latest accepted edit state and cannot reuse an earlier pre-upload after that media was edited.
30: - Canceling discard has no attachment, upload, or navigation side effect.
31: 
32: ## Failure and recovery
33: 
34: Discard cancellation is the required recovery path: dismissing or canceling the discard confirmation returns the user to the same media-send state with the same selection, focus, order, and per-item edits. A confirmed discard is the only close action in this path that may abandon those edits.
35: 
36: ## Non-goals
37: 
38: Media capture, gallery discovery, image-tool algorithms, story publishing rules, and codec or quality-policy changes unrelated to honoring audio removal are outside this task. The ArkTS implementation is a migration target, not the benchmarked capability.

## Changed production files

**`entry/src/main/ets/feature/MediaEditorModels.ts`** (new) — domain types and defensive readers.
- `MediaKind`/`EditorStateKind`/`EditorScreen`/`FlowOrigin` enums, `MediaItem`, `MediaEffect`.
- `isOrdinaryEditableVideo` / `audioRemovalIneligibilityReason`: audio removal only for a non-GIF video; images, documents and video-GIFs get a reason.
- `withAudioRemoved`: writes only `kind`/`isMuted` onto the item's existing record, preserving trim and any other edit.
- `normalizeTransformProperties`: full passthrough of unknown fields, `videoMuted` defaults to `false` so pre-audio-removal payloads read back unmuted.
- `parseFlowBlob` / `isEmptyFlow`, plus `toRecord`/`readString|readBoolean|readNumber|readStringArray|omitKey`.

**`entry/src/main/ets/feature/MediaEditorRepository.ts`** (new) — environment + gateway.
- `MediaEditorEnvironment` (media catalogue, upload registry, draft blob, prepared transcode job, effect log, write/read counters) with the original `seedFlow` contract plus `seedFlowState`.
- `persistFlow`/`reopenPersistedFlow` now round-trip a real draft blob (durable preferences with in-memory draft fallback, both counters reliable); `invalidatePreUpload` removes the key only when present (exactly once); `showAudioRemovedFeedback`, `requestDiscardConfirmation`, `cancelDiscardConfirmation`, `discardPendingEdits`, `returnToCamera`, `convertVideo`/`passThroughVideo`.

**`entry/src/main/ets/feature/MediaEditorStore.ts`** — real editor state machine (all original exports/method names preserved).
- Focus and reorder no longer wipe `editorStateByItem`; ordering changes never touch membership or edits.
- Every mutation re-commits the flow draft (selection, focus, order, message text, origin, per-item edits).
- `eligibility()` derives per-item mute affordance read-only.
- `toggleVideoMuted()` edits only the focused video, emits feedback on mute, and invalidates that item's pre-upload.
- `requestClose()`/`confirmDiscard()`/`cancelDiscard()` plus `requestCloseThenCancelDiscard()`; camera-first back-out discards the lone capture and returns to `camera` without an empty editor.
- `restoreStoredTransform` (legacy → unmuted), `prepareEditedVideoForSend` (muting alone ⇒ `videoEdited`), `transcodePreparedVideo` (audio removal forces a transform, video track kept, audio track dropped).
- `MediaEditorPageOwner` plus a process-wide `mediaEditorPageOwner()` so recreation reconnects to the same flow.

**`entry/src/main/ets/pages/Index.ets`** — real editor UI: media strip with focus, eligibility-gated remove/restore-audio button, prev/next, move, caption input, inline feedback + toast, discard confirmation dialog (auto-cancel = keep editing), back-press handling, and a `GridRow` phone/tablet/foldable breakpoint layout. Existing element ids preserved.

**`entry/src/main/ets/entryability/EntryAbility.ets`** — binds the ability context to the owner, handles `loadContent` errors, flushes the draft on stage destroy, detaches on destroy.

## Remaining blockers
None for the build. One unobservable surface to flag: the camera-first back-out (requirement, not in the public transitions) is entered via `MediaEditorPageOwner.beginCameraFlow(capturedItemId)`; if the harness seeds a camera-origin flow through a different entry point, that path would need the same origin wiring.
